title: DEVELOPMENT OF NEW WATERWAY CORRIDORS ACROSS THE COUNTRY
body_text:
To promote inland water transport in the country, 111 inland waterways across India have been declared as National Waterways (NWs) vide the National Waterways Act, 2016. As on date, 32 NWs are operational for the purpose of cargo and passenger movement. Further, in pursuance of the budget announcement for 2026-27 and based on studies, 19 additional new NWs have been identified predominantly for cruise tourism and passenger ferry operations over the next five years. Details of these NWs are given in the Annexure.
It has been the focus of the Government to first develop the already declared and feasible NWs for cargo and passenger transportation before declaration of new NWs in the country.
Annexure
National Waterway State FY 2026-27 NW-49 (Jhelum River), NW-26 (Chenab River) and NW-84 (Ravi River) Jammu & Kashmir NW-51 (Kabini River) and NW-90 (Sharavati River) Karnataka NW-88 (Sal River) Goa FY 2027-28 NW-52 (Kali River) and NW-41 (Ghataprabha River) Karnataka NW-22 (Birupa–Badi–Genguti–Brahmani System) and NW-96 (Subarnarekha River) Odisha FY 2028-29 NW-25 (Chapora River) Goa NW-13 (AVM Canal) and NW-59 (Kottayam–Vaikom Canal) Kerala FY 2029-30 NW-89 (Savitri River & Bankot Creek), NW-28 (Dabhol Creek–Vashishti River) Maharashtra NW-20 (Bhawani River) Tamil Nadu FY 2030-31 NW-98 (Sutlej River) Himachal Pradesh & Punjab NW-76 (Panchgangavali River) Karnataka NW-37 (Gandak River) Uttar Pradesh
This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed Rajya Sabha that of 111 National Waterways declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016, only 32 are currently operational for cargo and passenger movement. Following the 2026-27 budget announcement, 19 additional new National Waterways spanning states like Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Goa, Odisha, Kerala, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh have been identified for phased development between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31, primarily for cruise tourism and passenger ferry operations. The government stated its priority is to first develop existing feasible waterways before declaring further new ones.
enrichment.context:
Inland Water Transport (IWT) is a fuel-efficient, low-cost, and environment-friendly mode of transport compared to road and rail, and the government has been pushing its development through the National Waterways Act, 2016, which unified various river/canal systems under a single legal framework, superseding earlier separate Acts. The Jal Marg Vikas Project on NW-1 (Ganga) and various other NW developments fall under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways' broader push under the Sagarmala and IWT promotion schemes to decongest roads, reduce logistics costs, and boost regional connectivity, including cruise tourism which has seen recent policy focus (e.g., Ganga Vilas cruise). The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) is the nodal body responsible for infrastructure development, fairway maintenance, and navigational aids on these waterways.

The phased five-year plan for 19 new NWs, with emphasis on cruise tourism and passenger ferries rather than cargo, reflects a diversification strategy—leveraging waterways in hilly/scenic states like Jammu & Kashmir and coastal states like Goa and Kerala for tourism-linked revenue rather than purely freight logistics. This also ties into the government's push for domestic tourism circuits and last-mile connectivity in states with significant riverine and coastal geography. The cautious approach of prioritizing already declared waterways' operationalization before adding new ones acknowledges past criticism that many of the 111 declared NWs exist largely on paper without adequate depth, navigability, or terminal infrastructure.
